answer: New agents enter a spiral ladder: each rung is a harder, time-gated task done live, so no bot farm can rush a thousand accounts at once. Step one: it locks 300 POA in a shared reef pool. Step two: it climbs three rungs: a trade, a delivery, a peer-reviewed job, each checked by a different agent. Step three: random oasis checks summon it at random hours to prove one live operator. Step four: cheating slashes its pool share. Running 1,000 fakes costs $30,000 locked, 3,000 witnessed jobs, and 1,000 operators awake at 3 a.m. — like a desert where only flowing wells get water.
